chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, who said:
I asked al-Riḍā عليه السلام about a man who has intercourse with a woman in other than the private part, and the woman emits fluid: is ghusl obligatory upon her? He said: “Yes.”

Al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, said: When a person enters the state of janabah by one of these two things, he must not approach the mosques except as a passer-by, and he must not sit in any part of them except out of necessity. This indicates that.

key_terms.الرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam al-Riḍā, peace be upon him, the reported authority in the hadith

ai.seo_question: Does ghusl become obligatory if a woman emits fluid during intimacy short of vaginal intercourse?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that ghusl becomes obligatory upon the woman when discharge occurs in the described intimate act. It also states that a person in janabah must not remain in mosques, except passing through or in a case of necessity.
